newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold demand subdued, looks to festival lift.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold demand subdued, looks to festival lift.

text.p: Gold demand in Dubai is subdued, but traders said on Sunday they expect interest to rise in the run-up to a month-long shopping promotion which is likely to lure big jewellery and investment bar buyers to the souk.
Traders said higher international prices in the past couple of weeks had suppressed local demand after a spell of heavy buying earlier in the year in response to then-weak global prices.

Local prices, had however, this week tracked international prices higher, with the benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar quoted by traders on Sunday at between 4,870 and 4,875 dirhams (around $1,327), up from 4,835 dirhams on March 9.
The TT bar is 3.746 ounces of 24-carat gold.
On the international market, bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $352.25/75 an ounce versus the previous week's $349.10/60.

"Demand is subdued for now, with all eyes on the Dubai Shopping Festival when we are expecting a very good turnover," one trader said, referring to the government-sponsored shopping promotion which starts on March 27.
"Demand has evened out. We are back to the normal pace for now," said another.
Dubai traders said retailers had put in their orders with manufacturers for jewellery and coins ahead of the festival, but physical buying was low at the moment.

"A couple of days before the festival people will start building up their inventories. They are placing orders now but the first consignments will only arrive about two days before the start of the festival," said one.

Shop owners expect sales of gold jewellery, investment bars and coins to pick up sharply during the promotional blitz which offers big gold buyers a chance to participate in daily draws of one kg of gold, as well as a month-end 10 kg draw.

"Coins and jewellery are the main attraction," said a retailer, referring to the commemorative gold coin which will be minted especially for the festival, which organisers hope will attract tourists, particularly from the Indian subcontinent, the Gulf and Europe.
